results.content: Plug-ins are common for image- and audio-processing programs; they exist for such popular design tools as PhotoShop and Auto-CAD.19 Although commercial image and video editors may not support functions desired by researchers, artists, and designers working at the creative frontiers, a plug-in architecture enables users to extend editors with new custom functions. New software tools could be developed that would enable users to build their own software tools—collaboration between artists and designers and computer scientists could aim at a meta-toolkit that would offer ease of use plus flexible, extensible results, and an Internet-accessible repository of available software and hardware tools as well as guidance on what it takes to use them would broaden access and experimentation.23 Support for programming by people lacking full-fledged programming skills could be part of this kit.24 For effective development to take place, it is important to understand what shape the desired ITCP software will take—what interfaces it should provide, what functions it should support, and so on.

results.content: Once a course between Abu Dhabi and New York or Abu Dhabi and Shanghai is deemed as equivalent, students are able to use either of the courses to satisfy prerequisite and/or degree requirements without further approval needed. This is a full semester (or equivalent session) course during which students first learn the Arabic alphabet, then move on to work on the sentence and paragraph levels. This course builds on the knowledge and skills that students acquire in Elementary Arabic 1 (ARABL-UH 1110) which is a prerequisite course for this class. Students joining the course from outside NYU Abu Dhabi are [...]going difficulties in developing a global migration regime. The course introduces students to the ways in which a variety of actors and institutions at the national and transnational levels interactively contribute to public policy. In this course, students will engage with research on social hierarchies (race, class, gender, citizenship) in the UAE while exploring what it can look like to benefit the communities this research is about.
